<details>
The script `easycliproxyapi.sh` is a wrapper designed to synchronize files from a system-wide library directory (`/usr/lib/easycliproxyapi`) to a user-specific data directory (`~/.local/share/easycliproxyapi`). It ensures that the application runs with up-to-date core files while preserving user configuration and data. The synchronization uses atomic `mv` operations within the same directory to avoid race conditions, and file comparisons via `cmp -s` prevent unnecessary updates when content is identical.

All operations are confined to the package's own managed files: binaries, version metadata, and core assets under `cpa-core/`. User settings and persistent data outside these paths are explicitly preserved, as noted in the comment. The use of `flock` ensures only one instance performs sync at a time, releasing the lock before execution to avoid holding it during runtime. There are no network calls, no code evaluation (no `eval`, `curl|bash`, etc.), no obfuscation, and no attempts to exfiltrate data or modify system state beyond the application's scope.

The script follows safe practices by using strict shell options (`set -euo pipefail`), proper quoting, temporary files with `mktemp`, and secure cleanup via `trap`. All paths are predictable and based on standard XDG directories. The behavior is consistent with typical AUR packaging for applications requiring per-user copies of system-installed binaries or assets.
</details>
